text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to start, how would you describe the onset of this swelling—was it sudden or gradual?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia (likely Hemophilia B or A). The sudden onset of swelling in a young boy without trauma, combined with a specific family history of similar issues on the maternal side (suggesting X-linked recessive inheritance), strongly points to a bleeding disorder rather than mechanical joint disease.
